hypotheses.binder: (hf : MDifferentiableAt I I' f ((extChartAt I α).symm z))
hypotheses.justification: Write x := (extChartAt I α).symm z. After `inChartAt_apply` and `mpullback_apply`, the left side evaluated at v is ω (f x) (fun i ↦ mfderiv I I' f x (mfderivWithin 𝓘(ℝ,E) I (extChartAt I α).symm (range I) z (v i))). The right side is ω (f x) (fun i ↦ mfderivWithin 𝓘(ℝ,E) I' (f ∘ (extChartAt I α).symm) (range I) z (v i)). Proof: case split on `MDifferentiableAt I I' f x`. If it holds, the existing proof applies unchanged. If it fails, `mfderiv_zero_of_not_mdifferentiableAt` gives mfderiv f x = 0, so the left side is ω (f x) (fun _ ↦ 0). On the right, g := f ∘ (extChartAt I α).symm is also not MDifferentiableWithinAt (range I) at z. Suppose it were. Since x ∈ (chartAt H α).source (from `(extChartAt I α).map_target hz` and `extChartAt_source`), `mdifferentiableAt_extChartAt` makes extChartAt I α MDifferentiableAt x; this lemma uses the `[IsManifold I 1 M]` that is still present. Because extChartAt I α x = z (by `right_inv hz`) and extChartAt maps everything into range I (its coercion is I ∘ chartAt), `MDifferentiableWithinAt.comp` with s = univ, plus `mdifferentiableWithinAt_univ`, shows g ∘ extChartAt I α is MDifferentiableAt x. This function equals f on the open chart source, which contains x (by `left_inv`). So `MDifferentiableAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq` would make f MDifferentiableAt x, a contradiction. Hence `mfderivWithin_zero_of_not_mdifferentiableWithinAt` gives mfderivWithin g = 0, and the right side is also ω (f x) (fun _ ↦ 0). The two sides agree in both cases. Degenerate cases (k = 0, trivial spaces) need nothing extra, since the argument is pointwise and uses only the junk value 0 of mfderiv/mfderivWithin.
